title: Orchestration and unit-econ claims — field notes & sales scripts
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for the field and sales enablement team pairing performance claims (latency) with unit-economics claims (cost per inference) for mid-market and enterprise buyer conversations. The aim is to: 1) surface defensible statements we can make today, 2) give short proof points and artifacts a rep can attach, and 3) provide short scripts and objection responses for demo and discovery calls.

Status/context:
- Drafted after a week of benchmark syncs with infra and applied-ml. Data here is preliminary: numbers come from internal labs and a mix of hosted + dedicated perf runs.
- Not yet legal-reviewed; do not add to public site or press. Use in 1:1 sales conversations with conservative framing ("typical customers see...").

Top-level messaging decisions (quick):
- Primary claim pattern: "Lower median latency + predictable p95 with X% lower token cost vs managed endpoints".
- Use relative language for comparison ("up to", "typical", "vs standard managed endpoints"). Avoid absolute monopoly claims.
- Surface a small set of concrete scenarios (chat assistant, embedding-heavy search, batch reranking) rather than one-size-fits-all statements.

Defensible claim building blocks (what we can point to):
1) Observed latency envelope (hosted):
  - median (p50) generation time for 512-token context, 64-token generation: ~85–110ms/token on Redwood-hosted optimized runtime for small/fast models (internal avg).
  - p95 is sensitive to burst smoothing and batching; with our autoscaling+burst smoothing policy, p95 improves by ~30–40% vs naive autoscale (internal config).
  - Proof artifacts: latency trace screenshots (per-route in Console), small-sample p50/p95 tables attached in confluence:INF-latency-2025.

2) Cost per 1k output tokens (hosted + caching):
  - For steady-chat workload with high KV cache hits and batching, modeled unit cost reduction: 20–45% vs unmanaged single-node endpoints because of our batching + prefix caching.
  - For embedding-heavy, throughput-batched workloads: dedicated pools show 30–60% lower cost/unit vs on-demand GPUs due to utilization and reserved capacity.
  - Proof artifacts: benchmark run id: bench/2025-02-econ-v3 and token-cost breakdown from Console.

3) Multi-tier routing benefit (mixed latency/cost policy):
  - Example policy: route conversational QA to low-latency pool; route low-priority bulk embeddings to cost-optimized dedicated pool. Combined outcome: ~25–55% unit cost reduction for whole-app workloads while preserving <200ms median reply for interactive flows.
  - Proof artifacts: routing simulation CSVs + rollout logs.

Sales-ready micro-claims (short, repeatable):
- "We routinely reduce per-token cost by 30% for embedding-heavy pipelines through batching + dedicated pools, while keeping interactive flows under 200ms median."
- "Our autoscaling+burst smoothing narrows p95 by roughly a third in production-like bursts — that means fewer latency spikes during traffic surges."
- "You can pin model versions and routing policies, so experiments with quantized variants will never impact your critical routes."

Simple evidence pack to attach in early GTM outreach:
- p50/p95 table for 3 canonical workloads (chat, embeddings, rerank)
- Token cost comparison chart (on-demand vs reserved/dedicated)
- One-page architecture sketch showing routing tiers + cache layer
- Link to a sandbox demo that shows live console metrics (internal demo link)

Customer scenarios (short vignettes to use in discovery):
- Marketplace search (high-QPS embeddings): pain: skyrocketing embedding spend, unpredictable latency; ask: "What does your embedding spend look like in $/month and peak QPS?" Pitch: reserved pools + batching can shave costs 30–50% and flatten tail latency.
- Conversational product (chat UX): pain: visible stutters and occasional 2–3s replies; ask: "How often do your customers see >1s replies?" Pitch: route small-context interactive flows to low-latency runtime, keep p95 tight with burst smoothing and prefix caching.
- Enterprise compliance (private deploys): pain: must run on-prem but want same operational visibility; ask: "Do you need private network + single-tenant SLAs?" Pitch: consistent API across hosted and private — same rollout and tracing, with predictable capacity contracts.

Sales scripts & one-liners (short):
- Discovery opener: "What's the one latency or cost metric that would make this project greenlit at your company?"
- Demo setup line: "In this demo I'll switch routing policies — you'll see cost fall on the dashboard while the demo chat stays responsive."
- Close assist: "If we size a dedicated pool for your peak QPS, we can show modeled unit costs for a 3-month run and a small pilot to validate in-prod."

Objections & suggested framing (quick):
- "Benchmarks are synthetic": Acknowledge. Offer to run a short pilot with customer traffic or representative prompts and commit to sharing raw traces.
- "Cheaper sounds risky/low-quality": Explain tradeoffs: we offer quantized variants for cost, but default routing pins critical routes to full-precision variants; show rollouts/A-B and fallback policies in Console.
- "We already use batch endpoints": Ask how they manage cache hits and prefix reuse — often teams haven't optimized prompt design for caching; offer a quick eval to estimate cacheable fraction.

Competitive notes (differentiation and quick calls):
- Vs major cloud-managed endpoints: our claim is not "cheaper in every case" but "more predictable unit economics under realistic mixed workloads via routing + caching." Callout: highlight tooling that exposes per-route cost in Console.
- Vs self-managed open-source runtimes: we beat in onboarding and operational safety (rollouts, autoscaling, tracing). For pure lowest-dollar raw inference, self-hosted might win at high scale — emphasize our hybrid option (Private/Dedicated) and managed ops.

Open questions / data gaps (TODOs):
- Need verified p95 numbers for 1k concurrent chat users on hosted production traces (ask SRE for anonymized traces).
- Need example customer case study (embedding-heavy) we can reference publicly — flagged for CS to follow up.
- Legal to bless 3 templated claims and define phrasing for external use.

Appendix: quick examples to copy/paste into email sequences
- Cold LinkedIn opener (short): "We help apps cut embedding spend by ~30% while keeping live chat sub-200ms median — curious if that maps to your goals?"
- Follow-up with artifact: "Attached is a one-pager with a p50/p95 table and a short architecture sketch showing how routing + caching drive the savings. Happy to run a 1-week pilot with representative prompts."

Notes to self: keep this doc living in Drive; once claims are vetted by legal, create a distilled 1-pager for SDRs and a longer tech appendix for Solutions Eng.

-- Asha
